breakpoints.note: The key parser admits the witness into JSON-style quoted-key handling instead of the bare-identifier path. That quoted-key path is what allows `ucl_lex_json_string()` to flag escapes and `ucl_copy_or_store_ptr()` to take the unescape call at the scored source.

First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled malformed key state. On the vulnerable path, this in-place JSON unescape decodes a quoted key containing `\u0000` into an owned key buffer that now contains a literal embedded NUL while `ret` remains the full decoded key length.
The patch replaces this with `malloc(other->keylen)` plus `memcpy(..., other->keylen)`, confirming that the missing obligation is to copy key storage by explicit `keylen`, not C-string termination.
